guidebook.chemicalscience.chapter.introd: Chemical Science is an addon that aims to add many more recipes to Electrodynamics and its addons. It expands chemistry by adding ores, items, fluids, new tools, and machines. You can use it to learn a bit about chemistry too—everything is in the guidebook!
guidebook.chemicalscience.chapter.genera: "Chemistry is the study of change" - Walter White. More seriously, to understand chemistry you need to understand what an atom is. Matter, in general, contains atoms and energy. The energy is the motion of the particles inside of the atoms. An atom contains 3 types of particles: protons which have a positive charge, electrons which have a negative charge, and neutrons which don't have any charge. Like a magnet, protons and electrons attract each other because of the charge difference. Protons and neutrons are found in the nucleus, which represents practically all of the atom's mass. Electrons gravitate around the nucleus. The more energy they contain, the farther away they are from the nucleus, to a point where some can move away indefinitely from the atom. Here is an example of a Helium atom, with green for the 2 neutrons, red for the 2 protons, blue for the 2 electrons, and yellow representing the attraction between protons and electrons.

If you understand that the nucleus has the mass, the electrons can move away from the atom with energy, and that to be stable, charges must compensate, every aspect of chemistry can be explained from there.

There are at this time 118 different atoms known. But how do you differentiate them? The number of neutrons? It can vary from one to another and the atom still keeps its properties. The mass? If the number of neutrons varies, the mass does too. The number of electrons? Electrons are the interesting part of an atom because they explain most of its behavior, but if you kept track, I mentioned that electrons can move away. Then there is the number of protons. Because an atom must have as many positive charges as negative ones, protons will account for the stable number of electrons, as well as representing most of the mass in small atoms. That way, the periodic table sorts the atoms by the number of protons, which is why Helium is number two!

So, the order is the number of protons, but why does it look so chaotic? Well, nuclei have electrons orbiting around them, but you can't put 118 electrons on a single orbital without some traffic issues. So, to make things more complicated, atoms have multiple orbitals. An orbital isn't literally a circle around the nucleus but more of an area where each electron has a chance to be. For Hydrogen and Helium, there is a single one next to the nucleus, with two spaces. For an atom to be stable, the orbitals must be saturated in electrons. In order to do so, two Hydrogen atoms will go next to each other and form a bond, which is just sharing their single electrons with each other. In this way, you can deduce that the first row of atoms has one orbital, the second has two, the third has three, etc. The blue and green lines are part of the 6th and 7th rows, but the periodic table would be even more awkward if you shoved those two rows in between. 
And that is it for this chapter: atoms contain a nucleus which is most of their mass, electrons orbit around it, and for an atom to be stable, it must have a neutral charge and full orbitals.
guidebook.chemicalscience.chapter.organi: Organic chemistry is the study of chemistry focused on the Carbon atom. Life on Earth is carbon-based, meaning the element that constitutes the skeleton of molecules in plants, animals, fungi, and every life form in general, is carbon. But organic chemistry isn't just the base of biology, it is also the base of today's technology. Your phone, or maybe your computer, might have an OLED screen, which stands for organic light-emitting diodes. Why organic? Because it is made out of carbon, and that is why it is so good. Carbon electronics possess properties such as being extremely resistant to stretching, they do not use rare-earth metals, they are not toxic, and they can be way, way more powerful while consuming a lot less energy. I hope you know your chemistry or read the previous chapter; you will need it to understand this one.

The carbon atom has 6 protons and 6 to 8 neutrons. If it has 6 electrons, the first two will be located on the first electron orbital, like helium, and won't bond. The other four will do something called hybridization, which lets them bond with 4 other electrons. Carbon can bond with other atoms in 3 ways:

The straight lines are in 2D, in the same plane. On the carbon atom to the right, you can see 2 bonds in the same plane and 2 weird ones. The full triangle goes on top of the plane, the other goes below the plane. This is called the Cram representation (or Wedge-and-Dash), it represents atoms in 3D. The most used representation is called topology; it shows every bond without showing every carbon and hydrogen. For example, the molecule of Propane, which is 3 carbons bonding in a single chain, with hydrogens bonding with carbons in order to fill the orbitals, will look like this:

On the left is a classic representation, taking a lot of space, and on the right is the topological representation, where only the carbon-carbon bond is shown, and an angle is made, accounting for the 3D geometry of the carbon atom. Every molecule added by Chemical Science is in the guidebook, check it out!

We are going to jump a little bit in difficulty, because how the f* can this produce electricity? Well, it isn't simple. Carbon can make bonds with other atoms, but they can bond more than once. You know about Oxygen gas? Oxygen bonds two times with other atoms, so dioxygen is just two oxygens bonding twice with each other. If you remember well, a bond is just atoms sharing electrons. With a single bond, it is easy, it's just a straight line showing the region where electrons have the most chance to be in. But with two bonds, the single bond is still in the same place, and the second covers the single one.

In orange is a single bond, and in green a second bond. The carbons on the right bond two times with each other. The name for a single bond is σ (sigma) and for a double bond is π (pi). A triple bond would be one σ and two π. π bonds have the ability to move in the molecule. These two Bromobenzene molecules are the same, but the π bonds changed positions:

On top of that, this particular molecule also has a bromine atom, which has 6 electrons forming 3 non-covalent bonds that can move around with π bonds. The phenomenon of electrons moving in a molecule is called a conjugated system. There are 4 major types of conjugated systems: π-σ-π, which is the one in Benzene, consisting of π bonds covering σ bonds; π-σ-n, with n being a non-covalent bond; π-σ-ν, with ν being the lack of electrons of an atom; and n-σ-ν. A conjugated system's size depends on how many of these types follow each other. The bigger the conjugated system, the better it absorbs light, for example. This is why carrots are orange, because they contain β-Carotene which has a very long conjugated system.

You can see the conjugated system highlighted in purple, consisting of π-σ-π units. Those electrons are able to absorb light around 450nm (cyan), which is the complementary color of orange. Therefore, cyan is fully absorbed and the carrot emits the orange light it couldn't absorb. By absorbing light, the electrons move away more from the molecule (chapter on general chemistry), and can be used to make current. This is how an organic solar panel works: we use a polymer (a chain of the same molecule, repeating multiple times) with a conjugated system, and by repeating the molecule we increase the size of the conjugated system to make it absorb more and more light. In Chemical Science, we use Poly[3,6-bis(5-thiophen-2-yl)-2,5-bis(2-octyldodecyl)pyrrolo[3,4-c]pyrrole1,4(2H,5H)-dione-2,2’-diyl-alt-thieno[3,2-b]thiophen-2,5-diyl], which is kindly abbreviated as DPP-DTT polymer.
And that is it for the chapter on organic chemistry! I know it is complicated to understand anything without having done chemistry before, but I tried to make it comprehensible and not too long.
guidebook.chemicalscience.chapter.machin: The organic solar panel provides a lot more energy than the regular advanced solar panel. While it costs a lot to make the polymer, one polymer can make 10 of those solar panels. The organic solar panel also has the ability to turn invisible.
The circuit maker is a quality of life machine designed to make cirucit crafting easier, and less copper hungry. It uses rare materials to burn circuits.
The redox furnace is a power hungry furnace that uses low cost materials to process ores. Right-click with a wrench on the controller block to assemble it.
The fractionating column is a 13 blocks tall column capable of distillating crude oil. Right-click with a wrench on the controller block to assemble it.
The fume hood is the main machine used for organic chemistry. It can't be automated but offers a lot of possibilities. Right-click with a wrench on the controller block to assemble it.
The spin coater is used to turn solluble polymers into a film, making them usable.
The HDS unit converts petroleum products contaminated in sulfur to sulfur-free.
The catalytic reformer uses the sulfur-free petroleum products to make usable organic compounds, using steam and a catalyst.
The steam cracker uses the sulfur-free petroleum products to make usable organic compounds, using steam at high temperatures.
guidebook.chemicalscience.chapter.equipm: Organic night vision goggles give the player the ability to see in the dark. They differ from inorganic versions as they do not require charging and feature special modes to highlight entities and ores near the player.
The bulletproof vest is a sturdy piece of armor that massively reduces damage taken from projectiles. It is unbreakable.
The flamethrower is a weapon that fires a stream of flames at mobs. Damage and fuel consumption vary depending on the fluid used.
Tungsten tools are highly durable and mine faster than netherite, though they have poor enchantability and deal slightly less damage.
